scope: D9 limits of derived image representation, spatial scale, ROI pooling and engineering normalization revision

studies.read_level_this_stage: Previously reviewed primary full text revisited for feature comparability and processing limitations

facts.scope: MRI intensity normalization and feature comparability across prostate, brain and breast imaging datasets
facts.radiomic_evaluation: Compared radiomic feature equivalence across acquisition settings after different normalization methods
facts.finding_used: Radiomic comparability varied with normalization choices and acquisition context

studies.permitted_claim: Normalization choices affected radiomic comparability across acquisition settings, including brain imaging
studies.limits: Different images, software and feature definitions; not validation of our percentile transform or eight-feature panel. Do not infer that every feature changes under every normalization, that affine scaling necessarily changes our ROI-range fixed-bin-number texture values, or that the study establishes a cellular mechanism or tumor-change diagnostic performance. No inconsistent aggregate sample or feature counts from the article are reused.

own_study_claims.claim: All 546 supplied files use uint8 storage, unknown spatial units and matching relative grids; this is a computational grid check without independent anatomical registration validation
The positive-label ROI union pools supplied annotation regions without independently assigning tissue semantics to numerical codes
Unclipped scaling was an engineering amendment after clipping diagnostics, without diagnostic-label or model-performance selection and without preregistered or independent optimality validation
The model panel has eight FLAIR/T1post descriptors, no ADC, perfusion or physical-volume predictor

interpretations: Subsequent scaling cannot recover distinctions absent from already-derived intensities; no original acquisition bit depth or exact upstream conversion is inferred
Unknown spatial units prevent confirmed physical volume or millimeter neighborhood interpretation
Pooled source regions do not establish compartment-specific diagnostic performance or biological mechanisms

ROI-range fixed-bin-number textures may be invariant under positive affine intensity transforms; this does not establish invariance to clipping, arbitrary normalization, rounding or acquisition changes
Other processing conditions require evaluation; the cited normalization study does not validate our transform or panel
